title: Problem Header and Imports
content: File header documenting Erdos Problem #889 on new prime factors in consecutive integers. Imports `Nat.Basic`, `Nat.Prime.Basic`, `Nat.Factorization.Basic` for prime factorization, `Finset.Basic` for finite set operations, `ConditionallyCompleteLattice.Basic` for the supremum $\iSup$, and `Tactic` for proof automation.

title: New Prime Factor Count $v(n,k)$
content: Defines `newPrimeFactorCount n k` as the cardinality of $\{p \in \text{primeFactors}(n+k) : \forall i < k,\, p \nmid n+i\}$. These are the prime factors of $n+k$ that are genuinely 'new', not dividing any earlier term in the sequence $n, n+1, \ldots, n+k-1$. The filter uses universal quantification over `Finset.range k` to check non-divisibility at all earlier positions.
mathContext: $v(n,k) = |\{p \text{ prime} : p \mid n+k \text{ and } p \nmid n+i \text{ for all } 0 \le i < k\}|$

title: Maximum New Prime Count $v_0(n)$
content: Defines `v₀ n` as $\sup_{0 \le k \le n} v(n,k)$, using `iSup` over `Finset.range (n+1)`. This is the maximum number of new prime factors achievable by any shift $k$. The range is bounded by $n+1$ since for $k > n$ the primes of $n+k$ can only grow, but the finite range suffices for the conjecture's formulation.

title: Erdos Problem #889: Divergence of $v_0(n)$
content: States the central open problem as a `Prop`: for every $M \in \mathbb{N}$, there exists $N_0$ such that $v_0(n) > M$ for all $n \ge N_0$. This is the formal $\varepsilon$-$N$ definition of $v_0(n) \to \infty$. The statement is a `def` rather than a `theorem` because it defines the problem rather than claiming a proof.
mathContext: $\text{ErdosProblem889} \equiv \forall M \in \mathbb{N},\, \exists N_0,\, \forall n \ge N_0,\, v_0(n) > M$

title: Erdos-Selfridge: $v_0(n) \ge 2$ for $n \ge 17$
content: Axiomatizes the main result of Erdos-Selfridge (1967): $v_0(n) \ge 2$ for all $n \ge 17$. The proof uses the fact that for large $n$, among the terms $n, n+1, \ldots, n+k$, the term $n+k$ must have at least 2 prime factors not shared with any earlier term. This is the strongest unconditional lower bound known.
mathContext: $\forall n \ge 17,\, v_0(n) \ge 2$. Proved by Erdos-Selfridge (1967) in Illinois J. Math.

title: Complete Exception List
content: Axiomatizes the complete characterization: $v_0(n) \le 1$ if and only if $n \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 16\}$. These 8 exceptional values were determined by Erdos and Selfridge through explicit computation. The biconditional ($\iff$) makes this a complete classification, not just a sufficient condition.

title: Shifted Version $v_l(n)$
content: Defines `vShifted l n` as $\sup_{k \ge l} v(n,k)$, restricting the supremum to shifts at least $l$. Implemented as `iSup` over `Finset.range (n+1-l)` with index shifted by $l$. This generalization allows studying the growth rate when initial shifts are excluded, which may capture different arithmetic behavior.

title: Generalized Conjecture: $v_l(n) \to \infty$
content: States `ErdosProblem889General`: for every fixed $l$ and every $M$, there exists $N_0$ such that $v_l(n) > M$ for all $n \ge N_0$. This is strictly stronger than the base conjecture since $v_0(n) \ge v_l(n)$ (larger supremum domain). The generalization is natural because it asserts the divergence is not an artifact of small shifts.
mathContext: $\forall l, M \in \mathbb{N},\, \exists N_0,\, \forall n \ge N_0,\, v_l(n) > M$

title: General Implies Base Case
content: Axiomatizes that `ErdosProblem889General` implies `ErdosProblem889`. The proof is immediate: setting $l = 0$ in the general version recovers the base case since $v_0(n) = v_l(n)|_{l=0}$. This logical relationship justifies focusing on the stronger generalization.

title: Finiteness of $v_1(n) = 1$
content: Axiomatizes the question: does there exist a bound beyond which $v_1(n) > 1$ always holds? Erdos and Selfridge noted they could not even prove $v_1(n) \ge 2$ for all large $n$, making this a weaker subproblem of the main conjecture that remains open.
mathContext: $\exists B,\, \forall n \ge B,\, v_1(n) > 1$: only finitely many $n$ have $v_1(n) = 1$

title: Exact Power New Count $V(n,k)$
content: Defines `exactPowerNewCount n k`: counts primes $p$ where the exact power $p^{\alpha}$ dividing $n+k$ (with $\alpha = v_p(n+k)$) does not divide any $n+i$ for $i < k$. This is a refinement of $v(n,k)$ using $p$-adic valuation instead of bare divisibility. The `let` binding extracts the factorization exponent $\alpha$ for readability.
mathContext: $V(n,k) = |\{p \text{ prime} : p^{v_p(n+k)} \mid n+k \text{ and } p^{v_p(n+k)} \nmid n+i \text{ for all } i < k\}|$

title: Exact Power Shifted $V_l(n)$
content: Defines `exactPowerShifted l n` as $\sup_{k \ge l} V(n,k)$, the analogue of `vShifted` for the exact power variant. Uses the same `iSup` over shifted range pattern.

title: Exact Power $V_1$ Finiteness
content: Axiomatizes the exact power analogue of the $v_1$ finiteness question: does $V_1(n) > 1$ hold for all sufficiently large $n$? Erdos and Selfridge suggested this variant might be more tractable because the stronger non-divisibility condition ($p^\alpha \nmid$ vs $p \nmid$) is easier to verify.

title: Comparison: $V(n,k) \ge v(n,k)$
content: Axiomatizes that `exactPowerNewCount n k ≥ newPrimeFactorCount n k` for all $n, k$. If $p \nmid n+i$ then certainly $p^\alpha \nmid n+i$, so the exact power filter is more permissive: every prime counted by $v$ is also counted by $V$. This makes the exact power variant an upper bound, and its divergence would imply divergence of $v_0$.
mathContext: $V(n,k) \ge v(n,k)$ since $p \nmid m \implies p^\alpha \nmid m$ for any $\alpha \ge 1$
